From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>

Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-27T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Draft MAP + technical evaluation checklist

Anna —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our discussion, I pulled together a starter Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and a very lean technical evaluation checklist so the engineering and procurement teams have a single source of truth for the next 30–60 days.

Ask: could you confirm the names for the security and procurement contacts so we can drop them into the doc? That will let us lock the milestones and the procurement timeline.

What I attached/shared:
- MAP-template-v1.gdoc (link) — MAP sections include: stakeholders, acceptance criteria, data/telemetry plan, integration checklist, success metrics.
- MAP-slate-v1.gslides (link) — 3-slide exec brief you can use with stakeholders.

Proposed milestones (high level):
- Week 0–2: tech validation + API smoke tests (goal: sample infra + 1 model).
- Week 2–4: pilot integration + quality checks (acceptance criteria start to be measured).
- Day 30: pilot acceptance decision (go/no-go).

I assigned a few rough owners in the doc but we can update. Jasmine will own engineering readiness items; Marissa will coordinate the trial gating and acceptance slate.

Next step: when you share security and procurement contacts I’ll add them and schedule a 30-min kickoff next week to agree SLA targets and token/throughput expectations.

Thanks —
Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-07-27T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MAP + technical evaluation checklist

Jonas —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the concise slate. This looks like exactly what our stakeholders need. Quick answers:
- Security: Miguel Torres (miguel.torres@lumaflow.com) will be our security lead. He needs a SOC2 scoping note and the data-retention table filled out in the MAP.
- Procurement: I’ll loop in procurement once the milestone dates are firm; I attached our internal procurement window for reference.

I added two comments in the doc: one on expected latency/99p and another on a mock dataset we’ll use for validation. Do you have a recommended perf target to test against?

Would like to slot the kickoff for next Wednesday 10:00am PT if that works on your side.

Thanks,
Anna

I’ll pick up the engineering readiness section and add specific validation steps (API smoke tests, sample load, KV/cache sizing notes).

Jonas — can you drop the short perf target guidance so I can set the first test run? Suggested starting point: 200 RPS with 95% p95 <= 300ms on the sample dataset; we’ll tune after the first run. If that sounds high for them (Anna’s team), we can drop to a smaller baseline for day 0.

Also adding a one-page runbook for the pilot to the slides so they have a clear escalation path.

— Jasmine
